meta.source_title: A study demonstrating that using gravitational offset to prepare extraterrestrial mobility missions is misleading (Hu, Li, Rogg, Schepelmann, Chandler, Kamrin, Negrut; Journal of Field Robotics, 2025; author manuscript in NASA NTRS 20250001809)
meta.vehicle: MGRU3 (Moon Gravitation Representative Unit 3) VIPER test rover, four wheels, on the SLOPE lab tilt bed
meta.wheel_diameter_m: not reported for MGRU3 (the VIPER single wheel used in the lab is 0.50 m)
meta.bulk_density_kg_m3: not reported for the tests (Fig. 4a shows a GRC-1 range of about 1600 to 1820)
meta.friction_angle_deg: not reported for the tests (Fig. 4a shows a GRC-1 range of about 30 to 44)
meta.comparability_note: Markers found automatically as connected components of the black mask after a morphological opening (10 px) that removes the dashed and dotted connecting lines; the legend box is excluded and markers of the three series are told apart by component area (stars about 160 to 290 px, triangles about 340 to 390 px, circles about 600 to 650 px after opening), checked one by one on the overlay. Source plot has slip on x and slope on y; output x is slope and y is slip. Calibration on the light grey gridlines at slip 0 and 0.8 and slope 0 and 40 deg. Whole rover on a tilted bed, wheels driven at a constant angular velocity of 0.8 rad/s, slip from the steady translational velocity (Sec. 3.2). The rover digital twin used 88 kg to match these GRC-1 tests (Sec. 3.2); load per wheel about 216 N would follow (derived, not stated for the tests). The circles at slope about 0, 5.5 and 20 deg overlap triangle markers of the 2021 series and form merged blobs whose centres would be biased, so they are left out. Gravity offset rover at 1 g: the source argues such tests do not transfer directly to lunar gravity.
